about: T14 captions, written as a warm, clear tutor speaking; can be recorded as voiceover later. Times in seconds from the start of the lesson.

lines.text: Lesson fourteen: candlesticks. Open, high, low and close.
Almost every price chart you will see is drawn this way.
Here is one minute of a fictional BTC price, drawn as a line.
A line shows every wiggle. Now watch it squeeze into one shape.
That shape is a candle. It keeps just four prices from the minute.
Candles side by side make a chart.
A candle sums up one time window, such as one minute, with four prices.
Open is the first price. Close is the last. High and low are the extremes.
Think of one day's temperature: first reading, hottest, coldest, last.
Same idea. A candle is a price summary, not a prediction.
Let's watch a 1-minute candle form.
It starts at 60,000 USDT. That first price is the open.
Price dips below the open, so the forming body is red. The lowest point is the low.
Now price climbs above the open: the body turns green. Each new top is the high.
Until the minute ends, the last price keeps changing. The candle is not finished.
Time is up. The last price, 60,080, becomes the close. The candle is done.
Open, high, low, close: four numbers that tell this minute's story.
Let's name the parts. The thick part is the body, between open and close.
The thin lines are wicks, also called shadows. They reach the high and the low.
Body: 60,080 minus 60,000 is 80 USDT. Upper wick: 40. Lower wick: 60.
The range, high minus low, is 180 USDT. More than half of it is wick.
Up or down? Compare the close with the open.
Close above open: an up candle, also called bullish. Usually drawn green.
Close below open: a down candle, called bearish. Usually drawn red.
Same high and low, same 80 USDT body. Only the direction differs.
Colours are just an app setting. Open versus close is what counts.
Sometimes the close lands almost exactly on the open.
Here: open 60,000, close 60,005. The body is just 5 USDT thin.
That is a doji. Buyers and sellers ended the minute about even.
A doji does not tell you what comes next.
Four prices, but they are not free. Two rules always hold.
The high can never be below the open or the close. It is the top.
The low can never be above them either. It is the bottom.
Drop the close below the open, and the candle turns red.
Rule check: high is at or above both, low at or below both. Always.
One candle covers one minute. Put candles side by side, and you get a chart.
Time runs left to right. Price runs bottom to top.
Each new candle opens near where the last one closed.
The candle on the far right is still forming. It can change until its minute ends.
A common mistake: reading the top of the wick as the close.
Price did touch 60,200 in that minute, but it did not stay there.
The close is the edge of the body. On this green candle, the top edge: 60,040.
Wick tips are the high and low. Body edges are the open and close.
Your turn. Read this candle's open, high, low and close.
Is it an up or a down candle? Pause if you need more time.
Open 60,150 at the top of the red body. Close 60,000 at the bottom.
High 60,200, low 59,950. Close is 150 below open: a down candle.
Well done if you got it.
Before we move on, keep these limits in mind.
A candle shows what already happened. It does not predict the next one.
The last candle can still change. Big wicks mean fast moves and more slippage.
Nothing here is a signal. Waiting, or no trade at all, is always allowed.
Let's recap.
A candle sums up one time window: open, high, low and close.
Body edges are open and close. Wick tips are high and low.
Up candles close above the open; down candles close below.
Check yourself: a red body runs from 60,100 down to 60,020. Where did it open?
At 60,100, the top of the red body. It closed lower, at 60,020.
Great work! Next up: 1-minute, 5-minute and 15-minute timeframes.
See you in lesson fifteen.
